# Lotline: Data Provenance

<!-- GENERATED by `lotline provenance --write` from the download manifest and adapter metadata.
     Do not edit by hand: change the adapter's PROVENANCE block and regenerate. -->

Every dataset Lotline uses: where it came from, which version, when it was accessed, under what license,
how it was cleaned, and its known limitations (Participant Handbook, Data and Resources). Data is downloaded
by `lotline fetch` into `LOTLINE_DATA_DIR`, never committed; each download is logged with its sha256 in
`manifest.jsonl` there, so a pull can be verified byte for byte.

## Datasets

### Census 2020 geography: code files and DHC housing-unit parts

- **Source id:** `census_geo_codes` → table `none (inputs to eligible_parcels allocation)` (adapter `national.geoparts` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/library/reference/code-lists/ansi.html
- **Version:** 2020; publisher files last modified up to 2023-02-13
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 562 (5.1 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Read pipe-delimited files; build 7-digit place and 10-digit county-subdivision GEOIDs
1. A place is its own county subdivision when a subdivision with its FIPS code has class C*
1. Places with more than one county get 2020 housing-unit shares by county (DHC H1_001N)
1. Places that aren't their own subdivision get 2020 housing-unit shares by township (DHC H1_001N)

**Known limitations**

- Splits use 2020 housing units, fixed for every ACS year: homes are assumed spread like 2020 housing
- Housing units of all types are used to split one-unit detached homes

### Census 2020 redistricting data (P.L. 94-171): names and total population

- **Source id:** `census_dec_pl` → table `jurisdictions` (adapter `national.decennial` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/about/rdo/summary-files.html
- **Version:** 2020
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 56 (0.7 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Short names (before the first comma) and P1_001N total population for counties, places and county subdivisions
1. Joined to the BPS jurisdiction universe by GEOID

**Known limitations**

- Jurisdictions dissolved or renamed before 2020 keep their BPS name and no population
- Unincorporated county areas get no population (county totals would overstate them)
- 2020 counts carry Census disclosure-avoidance noise for small places

### Census American Community Survey 5-year estimates (B25024, B25003, B25064, B25077, B25034)

- **Source id:** `census_acs5` → table `acs_geo_year` (adapter `national.acs` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets/acs-5year.html
- **Version:** 2010–2024 (15 vintages)
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06
- **Files:** 615 (123.8 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Long format: one row per geography, 5-year vintage and variable, with the published 90% MOE
1. Census special-value codes become missing; a 'controlled' MOE (-555555555) becomes 0
1. Labels kept per vintage because some categories change over time

**Known limitations**

- Adjacent 5-year vintages share four years of sample: never difference them
- 0.3-2% of estimates are suppressed, mostly small places and townships
- Requires a free Census API key (CENSUS_API_KEY); the key is never written to the manifest

### Census Building Permits Survey (BPS), annual place-level files

- **Source id:** `census_bps_place_annual` → table `bps_place_year` (adapter `national.bps` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/construction/bps/
- **Version:** 1992–2025 (34 vintages); publisher files last modified up to 2026-05-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06
- **Files:** 68 (57.7 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Parse each regional annual file; ID columns found by header name (layouts change by era)
1. Keep units and buildings for 1, 2, 3-4 and 5+ unit buildings, both imputed totals and reported-only
1. Flag `imputed` when a place reported fewer than 12 months or reported units differ from the total
1. Assign GEOIDs: place, else county subdivision, else county for unincorporated/'County Part' rows; backfill earlier years by BPS ID (1992 on), then county + name, then unique name
1. Remove held-out place-years (validation/holdout.py) before the table is written

**Known limitations**

- BPS 6-digit IDs were renumbered in 1992 and reused; pre-1992 rows link by name only
- Before 2009, 0.07-2.9% of units belong to places that left the survey before FIPS codes existed and cannot be placed
- ADUs are often not recorded as new units (Upzoned #301); BPS may undercount them
- NC's BPS universe has ~157 places; most small towns' permits sit in county unincorporated totals
- Place sums exceed Census state totals in some years because Census revises state and county totals after the annual survey (BPS methodology); MN, NC, OH within 1% except 1992-93; TX 1-2% high in 2003-2014, concentrated in county unincorporated rows (e.g. Denton County 2014: +2,145 units). See reports/<st>/V0-national.md

### Census Building Permits Survey (BPS), annual state totals (reconciliation only)

- **Source id:** `census_bps_state_annual` → table `none (V0 check against bps_place_year)` (adapter `national.bps_state` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/construction/bps/
- **Version:** 1992–2025 (34 vintages); publisher files last modified up to 2026-05-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06
- **Files:** 34 (0.4 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Parse units for 1, 2, 3-4 and 5+ unit buildings (with imputation) per state and year

**Known limitations**

- Used only to check that place files add up; never an input to the model
- Held-out state-years are not compared, so a held-out place can't be recovered by subtraction

### City of Minneapolis CCS Permits (building permits, Dec 2016 on)

- **Source id:** `mpls_ccs_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.mn.mpls_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://opendata.minneapolismn.gov/datasets/cityoflakes::ccs-permits
- **Version:** 2026-10-14; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 159 (148.5 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** CC0 1.0 (City of Minneapolis open data waiver); CC0 1.0 (City of Minneapolis waives copyright in its open data)
- **Required attribution:** City of Minneapolis, Construction Code Services (open data, CC0)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Download the CCS_Permits feature layer (https://services.arcgis.com/afSMGVsC7QlRK1kZ/arcgis/rest/services/CCS_Permits/FeatureServer/0) with the ArcGIS pager into a dated snapshot (the layer is a rolling window from Dec 2016), requesting only OBJECTID, APN, permitNumber, permitType, occupancyType, workType, status, dwellingUnitsNew, dwellingUnitsEliminated, permit_Value, totalFees, issueDate, completeDate, comments where permitType IN ('Res','Commercial','Wrecking'). Applicant name, owner name and applicant address/city are never requested; Plumbing, Mechanical and Site permits are not downloaded
1. One row per permitNumber: a permit listed once per parcel it touches (about 3,700 permits) is collapsed to its lowest OBJECTID row, and its unit counts are counted once, not once per parcel
1. parcel_id: '27053' (Hennepin) + the 13-digit APN; for a multi-parcel permit, the lowest APN
1. issueDate / completeDate (epoch ms, UTC) → local Minneapolis calendar dates; issue_year from issue_date; date_precision=day
1. final_date = completeDate only for Closed permits, final_date_type=final_inspection (the item description defines completeDate as the passed final inspection); cancelled permits get no final_date
1. dwellingUnitsNew / dwellingUnitsEliminated (text) → units_new / units_removed; empty → null (unknown), never 0; units_confidence=reported when both are present
1. Wrecking permits: is_demolition=True; dwellingUnitsEliminated is always empty there, so a whole SFD wrecked → units_removed=1 (derived), any other building → null
1. building_type_std from occupancyType: SFD→SFD, TH→TH, TFD (two- or three-family)→DTQ, 3to4→U3_4, MFD→MF5, Comm and Accessory→OTHER, blank→UNKNOWN; when TFD/3to4/MFD/Mixed/Comm reports N≥2 new units the Census size class of N is used (2→U2, 3-4→U3_4, 5-6→U5_6, 7+→U7P)
1. ADU (type_confidence=inferred): Res permit on an SFD/TFD/Accessory occupancy; work type Accessory, Conversion, UnitCon, Remodel, Addition, UnitFinish, or New on an Accessory structure; comments name an ADU and do not negate it ('NOT AN ADU', 'FUTURE ADU') or describe work on an existing ADU (unless legalizing it); an existing house on the parcel (the occupancy is a house and the work is not a new house, the comments say 'accessory to a SFD'/'existing house', or the APN has another non-new house permit); and at most 1 new unit reported. adu_type from the comments (basement/attic → internal_conversion, garage/detached → detached, attached/addition → attached, else unknown)
1. ADU units: a permit typed ADU that reports 0 or no new units gets units_new=1, inferred (an ADU permit adds a home)
1. A new SFD/two-family permit whose comments name an ADU gets a second row (permit_id + '-ADU', 1 unit, inferred, no valuation/fees); if the house reports the ADU in its units (SFD 2+, two-family 3+), one unit moves to the ADU row (house row 'derived')
1. is_conversion=True for work types Conversion/UnitCon or when a permit both adds and removes units
1. valuation_usd = permit_Value, fees_paid_usd = totalFees (city fees and taxes; 0 kept as 0)
1. permit_class_raw = permitType:occupancyType:workType:status (status is kept so cancelled permits can be dropped downstream)
1. comments are read for the ADU rule only and never stored
1. jurisdiction_geoid = 2743000 (Minneapolis); held-out place-years removed (validation/holdout.py)

**Known limitations**

- Rolling window: the layer starts in Dec 2016 and older permits drop out; only dated snapshots keep them. 2016 holds December only
- dwellingUnitsNew is 0 on most ADU permits; ADU units are therefore inferred (1 per ADU permit), not reported
- ADU typing is inferred from free text: it misses ADUs whose scope of work doesn't say 'ADU'
- Cancelled, expired and withdrawn permits stay in the table (status is in permit_class_raw)
- Demolished units are unknown for anything but whole single-family houses
- A permit listed on several parcels keeps only its lowest APN
- Minneapolis only; Commercial permits cover apartments, mixed use and non-residential alike

### City of Raleigh Building Permits (Open Raleigh, daily, 2000 to present)

- **Source id:** `raleigh_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `ws-core-permit-text accuracy check (read-only)` v0)
- **Source:** https://data-ral.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/ral::building-permits
- **Version:** 2026-10-14; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 225 (244.8 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Open Raleigh Data Policy (public open data, no warranty; https://data.raleighnc.gov)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested fields exclude owner, contractor, address, coordinate and comment fields (no personal data)
1. Permits without an issued date (applications under review) are dropped; issue_year is the issue date's year
1. building_type_std from the Census BPS code in censuslandusecode (101 SFD, 102 TH, 103 U2, 104 U3_4, 105 MF5, 112 manufactured → OTHER); adu_type Attached/Detached/Internal ADU → ADU
1. Units repair: housingunitstotal is kept only where it fits the type code (1 for SFD/ADU/manufactured, 1+ for townhouse, 2 for duplex, 3-4 for 104, 5+ for 105; 0 never fits); otherwise SFD/TH/ADU/manufactured → 1 and duplex → 2 with units_confidence=derived; 104 and 105 without a plausible count stay null
1. Alterations, additions, accessory and nonresidential permits: units_new null (their housingunitstotal is the existing building's units, not new ones)
1. Demolitions (645-649): is_demolition, units_new 0, units_removed from housingunitsexist or the code (645 → 1, 646 → 2)
1. missing_middle flag copied to reform_flag_raw; censuslandusecode/workclass to permit_class_raw
1. Every row is assigned to Raleigh (3755000), the permit-issuing office, including permits issued in its extraterritorial jurisdiction (totals match the Census BPS Raleigh row within a few %)
1. Description fallback (lotline.parse.permit_text): where units or type stay unknown, the work description (proposedworkdescription) fills only that value, marked inferred: 104/105 counts that fit the code, units removed by demolitions, and the type of permits with no code; never overrides a reported or derived value; the parser's building_units is not stored
1. Holdout filter applied (NC holdout is Charlotte; no Raleigh rows are held out)

**Known limitations**

- housingunitstotal is nearly empty for permits issued from 2024 on, so most 2024+ unit counts are derived from the building-type code rather than reported
- Five-or-more and three-or-four family permits without a plausible reported count have unknown units (null). From 2024 almost every 105 permit is unknown, so 2024+ multifamily units are missing, not zero; the description parser recovers a count only where the text states one plainly (it is truncated at 100 characters, and project totals or two different counts give no count)
- Townhouse permits with no reported count are derived as 1 unit; the few that cover a whole building (4-9 units reported in 2023-24) would be undercounted when unreported
- The adu_type and missing_middle flags are populated only from 2019-2020 on; earlier ADUs and missing-middle projects are not flagged
- The catalog's '2013 anomaly' was not reproduced: 2013 new-dwelling counts match the Census BPS; implausible values are scattered (mostly duplexes reported as 1 unit before 2008) and repaired
- Alterations, additions and accessory structures are kept as OTHER with unknown units; an internal conversion that adds a unit is visible only when flagged as an ADU
- The city revises records in place (status, CO dates); each pull is a dated raw snapshot

### City-County of Durham All Building Permits (hosted ArcGIS layer, daily, Oct 2007 to present)

- **Source id:** `durham_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.nc.durham_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=c169c12616a54fcc99aac37ff4997a82
- **Version:** 2026-10-14; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 50 (37.7 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** City of Durham open data (Privacy Notice and Terms of Service on the Durham Open Data Hub)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Requested fields exclude owner, contractor, address, project-name, comment and description fields (PROJECT_TYPE and COMMENTS hold phone numbers and e-mail addresses)
1. Kept: permits with an ISSUE_DATE whose PmtStatus is not Void, Disapproved or Received
1. building_type_std from BLD_Type (Single Family House SFD, Townhouse TH, Accessory Dwelling ADU, Duplex U2, 3-4 Residential Units U3_4, 5+ Residential Units MF5, Mobile Home OTHER; Modular Unit with Single Family occupancy SFD inferred); a multifamily label contradicted by a reported count of 2+ is re-typed by the count (type_confidence inferred)
1. Units only for new construction (BLDB_ACTIVITY NEW): DWELLING_UNITS kept where it fits the type (1 SFD/ADU/mobile home, 1+ TH, 1-2 duplex, 3-4, 5+), else SFD/TH/ADU/mobile home → 1 derived, multifamily → null
1. Demolitions: units_new 0, units_removed from DWELLING_UNITS or the type (SFD/TH/ADU/mobile 1, duplex 2)
1. final_date = CO_SIGNOFF_DATE (certificate of occupancy); parcel_id = PIN15 as published
1. Jurisdiction by location: permit point inside the City of Durham corporate limits (CoD_Boundary layer, fetched with the permits) → 3719000, outside → 37063; permits without a point take the majority side of located permits sharing the longest 8-5 digit prefix of their NC PIN, then of their parent parcel (pending plats); the rest (~0.5%) go to the city
1. One row per permit number (a permit spanning several parcels is listed once per parcel)
1. Permits whose side can't be inferred (~0.5%) default to the city (Ben, 2026-10-14): ~92% of located permits are in the city
1. reform_flag_raw: 'EHC' plus whitelisted components (adu, duplex, flag_lot, small_lot) for permits whose PROJECT_TYPE starts 'EHC', fetched by a server-side filter; the text is never stored
1. Holdout filter applied (NC holdout is Charlotte; no Durham rows are held out)

**Known limitations**

- City limits are today's, not those in force at issue: a permit on land annexed after it was issued counts as city. Durham annexes most new subdivisions before building (utility extension), so the error is small but grows for older years. City-only figures therefore lean toward the city (single-family above BPS in 9 of 11 years): compare city + county with BPS until annexation dates are added
- About 3% of permits have no point; their side is inferred from neighbouring PINs (97-99.5% agreement on located permits) and ~0.5% are assigned to the city by default
- 5+ and 3-4 unit permits without a plausible DWELLING_UNITS have unknown units (null)
- Mixed-use and other Non-Residential buildings with apartments are OTHER with unknown units: their DWELLING_UNITS mixes in hotels, parking decks and project totals
- ADU permits filed as alterations, additions or other work (about 110) have unknown units: the permit may create the ADU or alter an existing one
- Duplex sides are often permitted separately (1 unit each), so permit counts exceed BPS building counts for duplexes
- The city revises records in place (status, CO dates); each pull is a dated raw snapshot

### FHFA House Price Index, annual all-transactions (state, CBSA, county, ZIP5, tract)

- **Source id:** `fhfa_hpi_annual` → table `market_geo_year` (adapter `national.fhfa` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.fhfa.gov/data/hpi/datasets
- **Version:** current
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06
- **Files:** 5 (137.3 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Skip FHFA's title rows; keep native HPI, HPI with 2000 base, and annual change
1. Prefix geography codes by level (county:27053, zip5:55415, ...)
1. Assign ZIP5 to states by USPS 3-digit prefix ranges (config/states); keep CBSAs touching the state
1. Suppressed years are left missing, never interpolated

**Known limitations**

- Sub-state annual indexes are labeled 'developmental' by FHFA
- Thin places suppressed: TX county indexes for 179 of 254 counties; 1-9% of tract-years missing
- FHFA overwrites files in place; earlier vintages survive only as manifest hashes
- Native HPI is base 100 in each series' first year; compare places with the base-2000 index

### FRED: 30-year mortgage rate (Freddie Mac PMMS), PPI residential construction inputs, CPI-U

- **Source id:** `fred` → table `market_geo_year` (adapter `national.fred` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://fred.stlouisfed.org/
- **Version:** 2026-10; publisher files last modified up to 2026-10-01
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 11 (0.2 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Freddie Mac PMMS, republished by FRED with permission; attribution required; Public domain (BLS, U.S. Government work); Public domain (Census Bureau New Residential Construction, U.S. Government work), via FRED
- **Required attribution:** Mortgage rates: Freddie Mac, Primary Mortgage Market Survey, via FRED (with permission)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Calendar-year means over complete years only (52+ weekly or 12 monthly observations)
1. A single missing observation between two published ones is linearly interpolated (Oct 2025 CPI)
1. Stored at geo national:US for every state
1. Also downloaded (not stored in a table): Census permits and completions by building size (PERMIT*NSA, COMPU*NSA) for the completion factors, via scripts/dev/completion_factors.py

**Known limitations**

- BLS published no October 2025 CPI (federal shutdown); 2025 CPI uses an interpolated October
- FRED revises series in place; raw copies are kept per month pulled
- The mortgage rate is Freddie Mac data: attribution required wherever it is shown

### Metropolitan Council Residential Building Permits (7-county metro)

- **Source id:** `metc_residential_permits` → table `permits` (adapter `states.mn.metc_permits` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://gisdata.mn.gov/dataset/us-mn-state-metc-econ-residential-building-permts
- **Version:** 2026-10-14
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 59 (28.3 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, Minn. Stat. ch. 13)
- **Required attribution:** Metropolitan Council, via the Minnesota Geospatial Commons

**Cleaning steps**

1. Download the 'Residential Permits' feature layer (https://arcgis.metc.state.mn.us/data1/rest/services/structure/Other_Structure_Public/FeatureServer/0) with the ArcGIS pager, requesting only OBJECTID, SDE_ID, CO_CODE, CTU_CODE, CTU_NAME, YEAR, TENURE, HOUSING_TYPE, RES_PERMIT_TYPE, BUILDINGS, UNITS, PIN, PERMIT_VALUE; address, ZIP, building/owner name and notes are never requested
1. HOUSING_TYPE SFD/ADU/TH/DTQ/MF5 → building_type_std of the same code, type_confidence=high (the survey records the type); anything else → UNKNOWN. DTQ and MF5 are never split
1. RES_PERMIT_TYPE gains (NU, MI, MU, FC, FS, FD, FM) → units_new=UNITS, units_removed=0; losses (RM, MO, TF, TC, TS, TD, TM) → units_new=0, units_removed=UNITS; RE (remodel over $1M) → both 0. Each row is one side of a ledger, so the other side is 0 by construction; a missing UNITS leaves both null
1. is_demolition=True for RM; is_conversion=True for the conversion codes (MU, TF, FC, TC, FS, TS, FD, TD, FM, TM); unknown codes leave both null
1. YEAR → issue_year; issue_date null; date_precision=year
1. jurisdiction_geoid: '27' + CTU_CODE (FIPS place code) when that place is in the MN jurisdictions table, else '27' + CO_CODE + CTU_CODE (county subdivision, e.g. townships)
1. parcel_id: '27' + CO_CODE + local PIN (punctuation removed; a leading county code stripped when the remainder has the county's local length; '0' placeholders → null)
1. permit_id: 'metc-' + SDE_ID (the layer's unique identifier)
1. Remove held-out place-years (validation/holdout.py) before the table is written

**Known limitations**

- Year of permit only, no dates; no permit number (SDE_ID is Met Council's row id, not a city's)
- City-reported annual survey; non-responding communities are filled from Census BPS without PINs
- PIN present on well under half the rows, and almost none in 2010-2014
- DTQ lumps 2-4 unit buildings; 5-6 unit buildings sit in MF5 with large buildings
- ADU recording starts in 2016 (C32): no ADU rows 2009-2013 and one in 2014 (fetch of 2026-10-14). Minneapolis ADUs 2016-2022 are about half the city's published count, so ADUs may also sit in SFD
- About 1.7% of rows are in county subdivisions not in the jurisdictions table (Carver and Scott townships, Empire, Credit River, Fort Snelling, Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community)
- Covers the 7-county metro only

### OMB core-based statistical area (CBSA) delineation, July 2023 (county to metro/micro area)

- **Source id:** `census_cbsa_delineation` → table `jurisdictions (cbsa_code, cbsa_type)` (adapter `national.cbsa` v1.0)
- **Source:** https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/demo/metro-micro/delineation-files.html
- **Version:** 2023; publisher files last modified up to 2023-08-04
- **Accessed:** 2026-10-14
- **Files:** 1 (0.1 MB); URLs and sha256 in `manifest.jsonl`
- **License / terms:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. §105)

**Cleaning steps**

1. Skip the title rows; keep CBSA code, title, metro/micro type and county FIPS
1. County GEOID = state FIPS + county FIPS; one CBSA per county
1. Each jurisdiction gets its county's CBSA (multi-county places: the county BPS files them under)

**Known limitations**

- Rural counties belong to no CBSA (no code)
- 2023 delineation applied to all years; CBSA boundaries changed in 2013 and 2023
